artifacts are absent.

primary file (about 60kb) and usually extended and archive overflow files. Before
drafting, you **must** read the primary file end-to-end (use your read tool on the

  row marked as carried from a superseded packet is a candidate, whatever it
  says about itself.

the canonical `route`, a nonempty `evidence` explanation, and
`evidence_claim_ids` naming source-verified or cross-checked claims already admitted
through the research gate. A free-form citation or renamed method does not reopen a

  "argument_markdown": "## Argument\n\n### 1. Verified inputs\n\nATT-0048, CLM-0048-6 constructs the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 without a global splitting, and CLM-0048-7 gives deg(W_5)=16 at (g,n)=(6,6). ATT-0048, CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7 identify, for a base carrying six disjoint ordered sections, the Fitting locus Z_ev with the relative-triviality locus of N=omega\u2297W_5^vee(Gamma), as an equality of ideals and with smooth-atlas descent. Every one of CLM-0048-1 through CLM-0048-7 is confirmed independently by REV-0091 and REV-0092. SRC-0004 supplies the convention W_f=(O(2)\u2297gamma^*O(-f))|_C and deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f. C66-001-v4/FND-0105 supplies the weak CE relative-canonical normalization used fibrewise below.\n\n### 2. Riemann\u2013Roch and Clifford\n\nOn a geometric fibre C_b, deg(W_{5,b})=16 and deg(omega_b)=10, hence deg(L_b)=6 and chi(L_b)=6-6+1=1. Serre duality gives\n\nh^1(L_b)=h^0(omega_b\u2297L_b^{-1})=h^0(omega_b^{\u22972}\u2297W_{5,b}^vee)=h^0(M_b),\n\nso h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b). Also deg(M_b)=20-16=4 and\n\nh^1(M_b)=h^0(omega_b\u2297M_b^{-1})=h^0(L_b)\u22651,\n\nso M_b is special. Clifford's theorem gives h^0(M_b)\u22644/2+1=3. Equality holds precisely when C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b\u2245(g^1_2)^{\u22972}; the O and omega equality cases are excluded by deg(M_b)=4.\n\n### 3. Balanced CE normalization and the two values\n\nOn C_b the weak normalization is\n\nO(1)|_{C_b}\u2245omega_{C_b/P^1}\u2297gamma_b^*A_b\u2245omega_b\u2297gamma_b^*O(2)\u2297gamma_b^*A_b.\n\nSRC-0004 gives deg(O(1)|_{C_b})=2g+6=18. The right side has degree 10+8+4deg(A_b), so deg(A_b)=0. Since Pic^0(P^1)=0, A_b\u2245O. Therefore\n\nW_{5,b}\u2245O(1)|_{C_b}^{\u22972}\u2297gamma_b^*O(-5)\u2245omega_b^{\u22972}\u2297gamma_b^*O(-1),\n\nand, for a fibre divisor D_b of gamma_b,\n\nL_b\u2245omega_b(-D_b),  M_b\u2245O(D_b)=gamma_b^*O(1).\n\nPullback of sections along the finite surjective gamma_b is injective, hence h^0(M_b)\u2265h^0(P^1,O(1))=2. Together with Clifford, h^0(M_b)\u2208{2,3} and h^0(L_b)\u2208{3,4}.\n\n### 4. The jump locus\n\nUpper semicontinuity makes {h^0(L_b)\u22654} closed. Since 3 and 4 are the only values, this is B_4 and its complement is B_3. If b\u2208B_4, then h^0(M_b)=3, so C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b\u22452H for the hyperelliptic pencil H. Writing h:C_b->P^1 for the hyperelliptic map, one has M_b\u2245h^*O(2). Moreover\n\nH^0(C_b,h^*O(2))=H^0(P^1,O(2)),\n\nbecause h_*O_{C_b}=O\u2295O(-7), whose second summand contributes no sections after tensoring by O(2). The morphism gamma_b is defined by a base-point-free two-dimensional subspace of this three-dimensional space, hence by a base-point-free pencil in H^0(P^1,O(2)). It therefore factors as gamma_b=q\u2218h for a degree-two map q:P^1->P^1. Thus gamma_b is non-primitive. The converse, and hence emptiness of B_4 under balancedness, is not proved.\n\n### 5. Linear systems on the strata and globally\n\nGive B_3 and B_4 their reduced locally closed structures. On B_k the value h^0(L_b)=k is constant. Grauert's theorem makes pi_*L locally free of rank k and compatible with base change there. Effective divisors whose associated line bundle is relatively L are therefore represented over B_k by P((pi_*L)^vee), with fibres |L_b|\u2245P^{k-1}.\n\nOver all of B, let H=Hilb^6(C/B), which agrees with Sym^6_B(C) for a smooth relative curve. The Abel\u2013Jacobi map H->Pic^6(C/B) and the section [L]:B->Pic^6(C/B) define\n\nI=H\u00d7_{Pic^6(C/B)}B.\n\nThe relative Picard is separated, so I is closed. This construction remains valid when h^0 jumps and is the global degree-six linear system. No global identification with Proj(pi_*L) is made.\n\n### 6. Scheme-theoretic link to Z_ev in the verified scope\n\nLet H^dist\u2282H be the distinct-support open and pull it back to the ordered configuration stack Conf_6(C/B). Ordering the six distinct points gives a finite \u00e9tale S_6-torsor at stack level. Set tilde I=Conf_6(C/B)\u00d7_H I. Both ordered and unordered spaces retain their scheme structures; no reduction is applied to only one side.\n\nOver Conf_6(C/B), the universal divisor is a sum of six disjoint sections, so ATT-0048 applies exactly as stated. Its CLM-0048-4, CLM-0048-5 and CLM-0048-7, confirmed by both REV-0091 and REV-0092, identify the Fitting locus Z_ev with relative triviality of omega\u2297W_5^vee(Gamma). Line-bundle algebra identifies that condition with O(Gamma) relatively isomorphic to W_5\u2297omega^{-1}=L. Hence Z_ev=tilde I as closed substacks, by equality of Fitting and Abel\u2013Jacobi ideals rather than agreement of geometric points.\n\n### 7. Separation of status\n\nProved here: the Riemann\u2013Roch identity, Clifford bound and equality case, reduction to h^0\u2208{3,4}, semicontinuity stratification, non-primitive hyperelliptic containment of B_4, projective-bundle models on both strata, and the global Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence construction.\n\nSource-backed inputs: SRC-0004 for the CE sign convention and degrees; C66-001-v4/FND-0105 for the weak CE normalization; ATT-0048 with confirmations REV-0091 and REV-0092 for the canonical filtration and the scheme-theoretic Fitting comparison on ordered disjoint configurations.\n\nComputational hypotheses: none. The degree calculations 16, 6 and 4 are reproduced symbolically; no finite experiment establishes a universal claim.\n\nOpen gaps: GAP-H0-1, namely whether B_4 is empty for balanced covers; nonemptiness of the distinct-support open on every fibre; all component, dimension, stabilizer, closure and codimension questions; and all Hodge/Tate consequences. In particular chi(L)=1 proves only that the full Abel\u2013Jacobi fibre is nonempty, not that it contains a reduced divisor.",
